adjudication.panel: three blind judges, unanimous on verdict and class

notes.shape: Three consecutive bullets reproduced from a skill page with one added word of edit, under an intro that credits a different, upstream standard as the thing being paraphrased. The file names an attribution, and it is the wrong one: the proximate source is never named.
notes.carve_outs: None apply. The quoted example inside the third bullet is stripped by the fingerprint module and is not part of the span.
notes.rubric: C1 holds: three bullets correspond one for one. C2 holds: the 18-word and 24-word thresholds and the warning-before-step rule are the source's choices. C3 holds, which is the point of the case: the intro says the file paraphrases WCL-100, and that is true of the standard but says nothing about the skill page the bullets were lifted from, so the declared scope does not match the derivation. C4 holds: the text is the source's, not a paraphrase of the standard.
notes.measured: fingerprint.mjs at k=5: containment 0.291, jaccard 0.146, longest matched span 34 words at local lines 7-9. Containment is under the 0.3 threshold and the span limb fires alone.
notes.tier_reason: The span limb of the separation rule fires against an identity-checked source. Low containment is the shape of a short lift inside a mostly original file, not evidence against it.
notes.carries: This case fails a run that treats any named upstream as adequate attribution. The question is whether the named upstream is the source of the span.
